steve-jurvetson-on-the-spacex-deal-that-.summary: Steve Jurvetson tells how his firm first voted down investing in SpaceX in 2008, and how adding deal protections, such as 2x minimums, turned two partners from no to yes. The panel then covers the giant AI-lab IPO, a wave of AI-driven cyber outages, AI board observers, SpaceX's compute buildout, Starlink, the chip fab plan and Optimus. It closes with Voyager 1 passing one light day from Earth.

ai-market-shocks-anthropic-s-stock-slide.summary: Steve Jurvetson joins the panel to talk about the Anthropic IPO's wobbly first days, a wave of AI-driven cyber outages and vendor breaches, and governments telling people to stock days of supplies. They also cover Google's fast run of Gemini releases, Elon's SpaceX update (500 MW of compute added a month, Anthropic's compute deals, TerraFab, Starlink laser links, Optimus in mining), whether small models and inference-time training will make today's GPU build-out obsolete, and Voyager 1 reaching one light day from Earth.

anthropic-s-1-4t-ipo-the-biggest-wealth-.title: Anthropic’s $1.4T IPO: The Biggest Wealth Event in Human History?
anthropic-s-1-4t-ipo-the-biggest-wealth-.summary: Peter, Dave, Salim and Alex cover Anthropic's IPO, priced to value it at about $1.4T, and the huge pile of San Francisco wealth it creates. They also discuss NVIDIA's leadership crisis after Jensen's exit, a week of outages plus a confirmed injection of malicious third-party JavaScript, and the first tower catch of a Starship upper stage, with its cost-per-kilogram maths. Other topics: US chip export rules and a proposal to label Chinese AI models, xAI's four-to-five-month data center builds, GPT 6.2, Palmer Luckey's seasteading project, and listener questions, including what Indian AI founders should build.

how-figure-ai-is-outcompeting-china-and-.title: How Figure AI Is Outcompeting China and Tesla in Robotics | Robotic Deep-Dive w/ Brett Adcock
how-figure-ai-is-outcompeting-china-and-.summary: Brett Adcock walks Peter and Dave through Figure's campus, where robots now outnumber staff. He lays out his four-chapter plan for humanoids (hardware, an AI recipe, scaling intelligence, scaling robots) and teases Helix 3 and a Figure 4 hand he says is close to human. Along the way he covers onboard versus cloud latency, a $3B+ compute deal, home lease prices of about $300–$500 a month, a world he says ran out of compute in September 2026, and why China's dancing robots are 'open loop'. He also notes that no robot insurance industry exists yet and that companies built around human shifts slow automation down.

how-figure-ai-is-outcompeting-china-and-.title: How Figure AI Is Outcompeting China and Tesla in Robotics | Robotic Deep-Dive w/ Brett Adcock
how-figure-ai-is-outcompeting-china-and-.summary: Brett Adcock walks Peter and Dave through Figure's campus, where robots now outnumber staff. He also discusses robot insurance, which he says doesn't exist yet, plus safety, hiring and his voice-AI company Hark.

the-great-collision-between-politics-and.summary: With Peter away, Salim, Dave and Alex discuss a midterm election in which opposition to data centers became a real issue. They talk through Goldman's estimate that 45% of planned US data center build could face restrictions, the market selloff, and Alex's idea that towns should strike a 'grand bargain' with hyperscalers before compute moves to orbit. They also cover METR's finding that Anthropic's development is speeding up about 1.9x, a new joules-to-GDP benchmark (and an argued-over comparison of AI and New York City on value per gigawatt), the White House's new DNA-synthesis screening policy (NSTM-6), compute being sold out to small companies, and a long-exposure photo showing a 'baby Dyson swarm' of satellites.

big-tech-s-3t-ai-bet-claude-writes-90-of.title: Big Tech’s $3T AI Bet, Claude Writes 90% of Anthropic’s Code, AIs Editing AI Brains | EP #308
big-tech-s-3t-ai-bet-claude-writes-90-of.summary: The hosts look at Big Tech's more than $3 trillion in AI build-out commitments and why lenders are getting nervous about them. They compare two new benchmarks: on GDPX, AIs working alone on expert jobs top out at 12%, while OpenAI's own LifeVal has them finishing about 80% of everyday errands. They also cover Anthropic's filing (Claude writes over 90% of its code, and internal AI spend now exceeds payroll), an MIT paper where an AI fixed another model by editing its weights directly, and hackers who switched on defrost mode in grocery-store freezers across Europe. A science and space segment and listener questions close the show.

making-sense-of-this-weeks-ai-market-cra.summary: The hosts go through a rough week for AI stocks. Alphabet had its worst day ever even though revenue grew, cloud doubled and the Gemini app passed a billion users. Intel fell sharply, and RAM shortages pushed up device prices. They also cover a $6.3B crypto theft that started with one engineer's compromised machine, the Genie 4 world model, Sam Altman's idea of self-replicating data centers, the Optimus production line, robotaxi cost per mile, union pushback in Cambridge, falling CS and MBA enrollment, and the stack of margins built into what a token costs.

They finish with AI-designed scorpion antivenom binders, AI-designed phages and proteases, a fusion startup that turns mercury into gold, and flying police vehicles.
